title: Le Blanc nodavirus Coverage Audit
eyebrow: LowVan · Le Blanc nodavirus module · 22 November 2026
h1: Does the Caenorhabditis nodavirus module actually work?
standfirst: The strangest genomes in the family. These worm viruses encode neither B1 nor B2; their capsid begins at a codon that is not AUG; and a −1 ribosomal frameshift fuses that capsid to a second protein which also exists on its own, from its own start codon. Three overlapping products come out of one 2.3 kb stretch of RNA2.

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: Four proteins, one of which has no profile at all.

blocks.html: Le Blanc nodavirus (49 genomes), Santeuil (44), Orsay (4) and Melnik (4). No ICTV genus covers them, so the module takes its most-sampled species' name. The margin is thin and worth stating: Orsay virus carries almost all of the literature below and has four genomes in BV-BRC.

RNA1 carries a single CDS. PMID 21283608 looked for a B2 and reported the absence directly: “All known nodavirus B2 proteins overlap with the C-terminus of the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and are encoded in the +1 frame relative to the polymerase. No open reading frame with these properties was predicted in the 3′ end of the RNA1 segment.” PMID 23468484 then found no silencing-suppressor activity for either Orsay protein proposed as one.

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: 98 training sequences, plus a nucleotide reference set for the protein that has no profile.

blocks.html: The capsid starts at a non-AUG codon. PMID 24503084 Edman-sequenced the mature Orsay capsid N-terminus as NKNNT and reports that it “corresponds to nucleotides 89–91, an AAC codon, which is not traditionally thought to be a suitable translation initiation site”, with “no AUG codon 5′ to” it in the segment. Checked directly on HM030971: nt 89–91 are AAC.

blocks.text:
verified on HM030971 (Orsay virus RNA2, 2574 nt)
     nt   89-  91   AAC      capsid start, non-AUG, Edman-confirmed
     nt 1255-1261   GTCAAAC  slippery heptamer
     nt 1262-1264   TAG      capsid stop, immediately 3' of the heptamer
     nt 1345-1347   ATG      free delta start

blocks.html: Consequences carried into the JSON rather than only into prose: upstream_ext is 0 on the capsid, because the annotator's scan_to_met_start would walk left looking for a start codon that does not exist; and check_met_start.py reports the feature in 100% of its members, which is the documented biology and not a defect. The initiation mechanism is explicitly unresolved in the literature and is not claimed here.

CP-delta is a −1 programmed ribosomal frameshift, so it has no PSSM. It is called from a curated nucleotide reference set in which one base is duplicated at the slip site. The transframe peptide was sequenced by MS/MS, and the protein incorporates into virions as a head fiber with a novel β-bracelet fold (PMIDs 24503084, 32817218, 28241071). RefSeq's join(89..1261,1261..2385) repeats nt 1261 because that is the slipped base — it is a frameshift, not a splice, and this module declares no spliced feature.

There are two slippery heptamers in this group, not one — and building on the published one alone covered half the module. With Orsay's G_UCA_AAC as the only constraint, 24 references were built from Le Blanc and Orsay, and 23 genomes reported no insertion sits in the slip site — every Santeuil and Melnik genome. Reading the 7 nucleotides immediately 5′ of the capsid stop in each genome separates them exactly by species: Orsay and Le Blanc carry GTCAAAC in 26 of 26; Santeuil and Melnik carry GGAAAAC in 24 of 24. PMID 24503084 notes only that Le Blanc shares Orsay's slippery sequence and Santeuil's differs, without giving Santeuil's.

blocks.text:
reference set, both heptamers
     references written                               47
     slip site confirmed at the insertion             47
     reproduces its own deposited fusion protein      47   (byte-for-byte)
     species covered     Le Blanc 26, Santeuil 22, Melnik 2, Orsay 1

blocks.html: Free delta is a separate initiation, and it is real. It has its own AUG at RNA2 nt 1345 and is 332–398 aa. PMID 29743360 settled it with an ATG→CTG mutant that still makes normal CP-delta but no free delta and has a non-lytic egress defect. It is absent from RefSeq NC_028098.1 and present only in HM030971.2, which is why only three deposits exist — the collection was expanded by extraction, and 46 of 46 extracted members are exact C-terminal substrings of the fusion from their own genome, beginning at fusion residue 419–434 (Orsay's published 420 among them).

sections.title: Where the cutoffs sit
sections.lede: Raised from 19 panel genomes, and re-measured afterwards.

rows: no profile; called from nucleotide references

blocks.html: Each cutoff is half the lowest score among the feature's genuine panel calls, capped at 500. Re-measured after the raise, every feature still calls on 100% of routed genomes and all 19 panel genomes are still graded good.

sections.title: Does it route?
sections.lede: Seven references, every genome in the group.

items: rep contigs, against a budget of 25
best hit from any other module

blocks.html: All four species contribute references, including Melnik, whose deposits are partial at both ends and carry no complete CDS. A reference only has to be a BLASTn subject, so a partial genome can still route its relatives even when it cannot itself be fully annotated.

sections.title: Does it call the proteins?
sections.lede: 65 genomes carry calls; 19 carry two complete, distinct segments.

blocks.html: CP-delta is called on every complete genome in the panel. That number cannot come from the flat feature table, which has no representation for a special feature at all — it comes from the full GTO pipeline, which runs the transcript-edit caller. A module with a frameshift product scored from the feature table would report that product as simply absent, with nothing to flag it.
Across all 65 genomes carrying any call, the replicase reaches 75% and the RNA2 products 77%, the shortfall being single-segment deposits that cannot carry the other segment's genes.

sections.title: Are the calls right?
sections.lede: Coordinates against the deposited record, including the non-AUG start.

blocks.html: Orsay virus RNA2 (HM030971) is called at exactly the coordinates deposited, including the start codon that is not a start codon:

blocks.text:
CP      89-1264    391 aa    begins at the AAC codon, no AUG upstream
  delta 1345-2385    346 aa    begins at its own ATG

  both exactly as annotated on HM030971.2

blocks.html: Every nesting reported is declared architecture: the capsid and free delta both sit inside the fusion, because the fusion is the capsid plus a frameshift plus delta. qc_cross_feature.py reports them as 100%-identical collisions, which is true by construction; audit_bins.py, which accepts a declaration, reads Unresolved: 0 with those pairs declared. The fusion itself has no profile, so there is no profile for the capsid to compete with.

sections.title: What it cannot do
sections.lede: Two real limits, one of them a direct consequence of how the deposits were made.

blocks.html: 1. Santeuil and Melnik RNA2 deposits are 5′-truncated, and are excluded from the capsid collection. Their contigs begin inside the capsid gene, so the encoded proteins start at Lys rather than the Edman-verified Asn — 22 of 50 capsid deposits. Training a profile on them would place the capsid N-terminus 15 residues late in every genome it called. They are excluded rather than trimmed, which costs Santeuil representation in that one feature; its frameshift references are unaffected, because a reference only has to span the slip site.

2. The non-AUG start is annotated as a fact, not explained as a mechanism. The 2014 paper floats an upstream UUG at nt 56–58 followed by proteolysis, then argues against it — the UUG “lacks a strong initiation context” and Santeuil has an in-frame stop five codons upstream — and prefers initiation directly at the NKNNT site “via some unknown mechanism”. The module records the verified N-terminus and claims nothing about how the ribosome gets there.

3. Melnik nodavirus has no complete CDS and no RefSeq (MK774657–MK774660, two isolates, both ends open). It contributes a routing reference and two frameshift references, and it will not produce a complete annotation from the records that exist.

A trap defused rather than a limit. Santeuil's RefSeq NC_015070.1 labels the fusion protein delta and gives the capsid a /note="protein A". So one string covers both a 765 aa fusion and a ~346 aa free protein, and protein A appears on an RNA2 capsid. Length routing separates the first; protein A binds nothing in this module and is left to the homology rescue.

sections.title: What the run found
sections.lede: Genome quality from the full GTO pipeline, which is the only path that sees the frameshift.

blocks.html: A, CP and DELTA carry copy_num. CP_DELTA deliberately does not, and never can: a special feature is emitted by a different program from the one that scores genome quality, so marking it essential would flag genomes on the basis of a measurement the quality step never makes.

One apparent miss was an artefact of merging. Santeuil 977913.15 appeared to lack the capsid, the fusion and delta — but it is MN131015 + MN131016, both 2,896 nt and both the polymerase, merged into a 5,792 nt “genome” with no capsid segment at all. It would have withheld copy_num from three features on the strength of an artefact. A length window cannot catch it, because this module's two segment windows are 2896–3628 and 2525–2937, so a pair of 2,896 nt polymerases satisfies both. Each contig is now assigned to a segment by homology to the module's own collections.

sections.title: What the vocabulary bought
sections.lede: Four annotation strings, two of them new, across four species.

blocks.html: The collapse ratio is the lowest of the four modules, and for a good reason: this group was sequenced by a small number of laboratories over a short period, so its source vocabulary is already fairly disciplined. The fusion protein still arrives under two names — alpha-delta fusion protein and capsid-delta fusion protein — because submitters disagree about whether to call the capsid alpha.

Two strings are new to the LowVan vocabulary: Capsid-delta fusion protein and Nonlytic egress protein delta. The second names a function the literature establishes directly (PMID 29743360) rather than falling back on an uncharacterized form, and the first describes what the protein is rather than how it is made.
